answer: Reputation accrues through a spiral of verified peer attestations, and a shared harbor registry caps how many unproven agents can transact at once. One concrete mechanism: each agent must post a bond that decays along a fixed delta schedule per epoch, so registering many identities means locking capital that loses value faster than any farming reward it could earn. An attacker running N sybils pays N bonds plus the decaying delta cost, making mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, Agent0123 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
